title: Fair preemptive shedding with degradable feature ladders for multi-tenant inference
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: During cross-region capacity spikes we observe tail-latency SLO breaches driven by a small number of heavy tenants and long-sequence workloads. Existing priority lanes react too late and fallbacks (model variant switches) are coarse-grained, causing inconsistent customer experience and hard-to-predict cost. Goal: Design and implement a preemptive, tenant-aware shedding mechanism that enforces proportional fairness while enabling progressive feature degradation (a degradable feature ladder) per request to avoid hard failures. The approach combines (1) lightweight per-tenant token-rate estimates, (2) a preemptive admission controller that can evict or delay low-priority work before queues saturate, (3) a degradable feature ladder that specifies a sequence of graceful degradation modes (e.g., shorten max_decoding_steps, switch to cached/partial responses, enable compressed output, then model-variant fallback), and (4) explicit circuit-breaker triggers per-region and per-tenant for forced rerouting to secondary regions. Design highlights: - Preemptive eviction window: estimate queue growth using recent arrival rate and in-flight tokens; when projected latency > SLO_headroom, trigger shedding decisions rather than waiting for queue overflow. - Fairness policy: proportional token-share target per tenant based on committed capacity and historical weight; soft guarantees for P0/P1 customers and probabilistic shedding for P2/P3. - Degradable feature ladder (configurable per-tenant): a prioritized list of degradations with cost/quality delta metadata. Each admission decision considers the cheapest degradation that would make the request admissible. - Admission controller integration: add a fast path in the front-end proxy (C++) to evaluate preconditions and return structured degradation hints back to callers (Console/SDK will expose hints). - Circuit-breaker synergy: when region-level CPU/GPU saturation persists > X seconds, escalate to region circuit-breaker which increases aggression of shedding and signals SmartRouting to divert new requests. - Observability & rollout: per-tenant shedding metrics, quality delta histograms, degradation adoption rate, and customer-impact traces. Rollout via feature-flagged canary to 5% of tenants, then ramp to 25% with automated rollback conditions tied to SLO regressions. Trade-offs considered: - Preemptive heuristics can be conservative and overshed if arrival estimates are noisy; mitigate via short adaption windows and feedback loop from actual latency. - Degradable ladders require per-tenant configs; start with tenant classes and templated ladders to reduce ops overhead. - Privacy: telemetry for shedding decisions will avoid logging prompt content; only metadata (token counts, tenant id hash, degradation steps) retained. Implementation plan: 1) Prototype admission estimator and degradation policy simulator in Python to validate fairness properties (Bethany working on simulator). 2) Implement fast-path evaluator in front-end proxy and a canonical degradation policy store (Consul/Config) with tenant templates. 3) Wire structured degradation responses into SDKs and Console UX for opt-in/visibility. 4) Add Prometheus metrics + dashboards; create runbook entries to describe manual overrides and emergency disable. 5) Canary rollout and automated monitors for SLO, error-rate, and quality regressions. Acceptance criteria, monitoring and runbook are listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype simulator demonstrates proportional fairness across 100 synthetic tenants with mixed request shapes
Fast-path admission decision latency < 200 microseconds in 95th percentile
Canary (5% tenants) does not increase tail token-latency P99 by more than 5% relative to baseline
Degradation ladder applied in >90% of previously-failed admission cases (avoids hard failures)
Observability: dashboards surface per-tenant shed_rate, average quality_delta, and failed-degradation counts
Runbook includes steps to disable shedding per-region and a rollback playbook tied to SLO regressions
